signals.title: The government is claiming a big pothole win, but can you tell the difference?
signals.summary: The government says nearly 7,000 miles of road will be resurfaced this year, but will its £7.3 billion pothole funding package make Britain's roads any better for motorcyclists? The government says its pothole repair programme is delivering smoother roads, with new figures showing an increase in resurfacing work and billions of pounds being spent on road maintenance. Whether that translates into a noticeably better experience for motorcyclists is another question. Figures published by the Department for Transport (DfT) on 21 October claim that nearly 7,000 miles of road will have beeen resurfaced across England during 2026, a 10 per cent increase on the previous year. The government also says that local authorities are set to spend a combined £4.9 billion on road maintenance this year, representing an increase of £800 million compared with the period before the current government came to power. Alongside the figures, the DfT has released another £220 million in incentive-based funding for councils that meet performance targets, with further money dependent on councils meeting additional requirements. Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander said the figures show that the government is beginning to turn a corner on the country's pothole problem, although she acknowledged that there is still plenty of work to do. For motorcyclists, however, the headline figures only tell part of the story. The government says its £7.3 billion road maintenance funding package is helping motorists avoid repair bills, with the potential for the average driver to save almost £600 through reduced vehicle damage. That figure is a government estimate rather than a guaranteed saving, and the announcement doesn’t establish how much of the claimed benefit will be felt by motorcyclists specifically. Nor does resurfacing mileage, on its own, tell us whether the roads being worked on are the ones that most need attention. A freshly resurfaced stretch of carriageway is welcome, but the total mileage figure does not reveal how many dangerous potholes have been eliminated, how long repairs are expected to last or whether problem roads are being prioritised. Those are important points for riders, as a pothole, or badly repaired section of tarmac, can be a more immediate hazard than it is for someone travelling in a car. The DfT's latest figures do offer some indication that councils are changing their approach to maintenance. According to the department, 94 per cent of councils will carry out preventative roadworks this year, compared with 76 per cent last year. Preventative maintenance is intended to address deterioration before it develops into more expensive repairs and dangerous hazards, rather than repeatedly patching the same section of road after potholes appear. In principle, that's good for bikers, and should be a more effective way of maintaining the network. What the new figures don’t show is how much difference it will make to road conditions over the longer term. The government also points to separate figures covering the year ending March 2026, which it says show an improvement in local road conditions, with fewer minor roads requiring maintenance following work carried out during the previous year. The additional funding and increased resurfacing activity are welcome developments if they result in better-maintained roads. But the announcement leaves some important questions unanswered for riders. There’s no breakdown in the headline figures showing how much of the additional spending is being directed towards roads with high motorcycle traffic, or how many potholes have been repaired against how many claims for damage caused by road defects have been made. There is also a difference between resurfacing a road and ensuring that its surface remains suitable for motorcycling. Loose chippings, uneven joins, degraded edges and poorly reinstated utility trenches can all affect the quality of a ride, even where a council can legitimately count maintenance work as completed. The additional £220 million is also tied to performance-based targets, with the government saying funding can be withheld from councils that fail to meet the requirements. That introduces a degree of accountability, but the effectiveness of the approach will depend on what councils are required to deliver and how consistently their performance is assessed. For now, the government's figures suggest that more money is being spent and more resurfacing work is planned. Ultimately, though, the measure of success will not be how many miles of tarmac appear in a government announcement, but whether the condition of Britain's roads improves in a way that people using them can actually see and feel. signals.title: Motorcyclist jailed after GoPro captures 130mph Ninja H2 police escape
signals.summary: GoPros recorded Amin Belechguer as he fled from the police. He later scampered through hedge rows after officers disabled his bike. A motorcyclist has been jailed after footage recorded on his own GoPro camera was used as evidence against him in court, showing him riding at excessive speeds and repeatedly ignoring basic road safety rules. Amin Belechguer, 29, of Poynders Gardens, Clapham, South London, fled from police in 2025. However, although he initially escaped capture, officers seized his supercharged Kawasaki Ninja H2, along with his GoPro camera and mobile phone, providing evidence that would later be used against him. The recovered footage showed Belechguer travelling at more than twice the speed limit on motorways and through town centres, performing wheelies and what Kent Police described as ‘dangerous manoeuvres’. He was also filmed running red lights, racing other vehicles at car meets, and riding along pavements and across pedestrian crossings. According to Kent Police, the incident that led to his arrest began when a patrol car, already responding to another call-out with its blue lights and sirens activated, was travelling along the A20 Ashford Road towards Maidstone. Belechguer pulled out in front of the police car before turning towards the officers and waving, apparently attempting to provoke them into a pursuit. Officers pursued the rider for a short time, during which he reportedly reached speeds of more than 130mph. He also crossed solid white centre lines and rode towards oncoming traffic over the blind brow of a hill. The officers eventually dropped back to reduce the risk of a collision, while colleagues further along the road deployed a stinger device in an attempt to puncture the Ninja H2's tyres. With the tyres deflated, Belechguer abandoned the motorcycle and ran into nearby hedgerows in an attempt to evade capture. Although he initially escaped, the motorcycle and the recording equipment left at the scene provided investigators with evidence of his riding. The 29-year-old pleaded guilty to the offences and was sentenced at Maidstone Crown Court on Wednesday, 21 October 2026. In addition to his custodial sentence, the Kawasaki Ninja H2 was made subject to a forfeiture order and will be permanently confiscated. Belechguer will also face a 10-year driving ban upon his release from custody. Speaking about the case, investigating officer PC Daniel Goodman said: “Officers worked swiftly when presented with the opportunity to arrest a dangerous motorist. Despite having to terminate a pursuit due to the dangerousness of Belechguer’s driving, teamwork saw his vehicle brought to a stop and secured his arrest. “Not only did Belechguer drive at triple the speed limit in some instances, but he demonstrated little regard for basic road safety when he failed to adhere to road markings, signage and traffic lights. “Throughout the investigation, Belechguer showed no remorse for the fact he placed his life and the lives of other road users at risk on numerous occasions. The DVLA is considering changes to the way vehicle number plates are supplied in the UK, raising questions about whether the review could have implications for motorcycle plate sellers and riders. The proposals are outlined in the agency's Business Plan for 2026 to 2027, published on 19 October, which says it will consider ways to strengthen the number plate supply regime as part of its work to tackle illegal plates. Among the measures under consideration are tighter checks on number plate suppliers, improved intelligence sharing, potential changes to fees and closer cooperation with police forces and Trading Standards. The plan does not set out any new restrictions specifically targeting motorcycle number plates, nor does it announce changes to the existing rules governing the plates riders can legally display. However, the review could have implications for businesses involved in supplying registration plates, depending on how the proposals develop. The move comes amid wider government efforts to tackle the use of illegal number plates, including so-called ghost plates, which can be designed to make registration characters more difficult for cameras to read, as well as undersized ‘show plates’. In a written parliamentary answer on 14 October, the Department for Transport confirmed that the DVLA was considering options for a more robust and auditable Register of Number Plate Suppliers. These could involve changes to the scheme's fees, structure, resources and funding. The Government has also been working on amendments to the British Standard for number plates intended to prohibit raised or ghost characteristics and require finished plates to be flat. Work to bring those amendments into law is under way, according to the parliamentary response. Separate proposals being considered by the Government include introducing penalty points and vehicle seizure for people in charge of vehicles displaying incorrect, altered or false number plates. A consultation on those measures closed in May, with responses still being considered. signals.summary: Adventure Bike Rider is bringing a slice of its summer festival to Motorcycle Live this November, complete with practical sessions and a few familiar festival attractions. Adventure Bike Rider (ABR) is bringing its own festival atmosphere to MCL26, with a dedicated ABR Festival Zone planned for the NEC in Birmingham from 21 to 29 November. Located in Hall 3, the zone will recreate elements of the ABR Festival, swapping the usual campsite setting for an indoor programme of adventure motorcycling talks, practical sessions and entertainment across all nine days of the show. At the centre of the area will be the Traveller's Tales tent, hosting a programme of talks featuring a number of established names from the adventure riding scene. Visitors will be given silent disco headphones to listen to the talks, with festival playlists available between sessions. signals.title: Dainese the disruptor? Smart GO airbag system set to shake up the sector
signals.summary: The Dainese Smart GO motorcycle airbag vest weighs 780g and offers Level 2 chest and back protection, with smartphone power and optional backpack integration. Dainese’s new electronic airbag weighs 780g, offers Level 2 chest and back protection and can be powered by a compatible smartphone, removing the need for a conventional charging routine. Priced at £329 in the UK, Dainese is hoping that Smart GO will be both simpler to use and more affordable than a traditional airbag system, thanks to some innovative first-in-class features. The new system tips the scales at just 780g, including its gas generator, making it one of the lightest products of this kind on the market by some margin. It’s designed to be worn over or under motorcycle clothing, as well as casual jackets. It features adjustable straps allowing a single size to accommodate different body shapes, while its packable construction means it can be stowed in a backpack, motorcycle luggage or under a scooter seat when not in use. The vest provides Level 2 protection for both the chest and back under the EN 1621-4 standard, with Dainese claiming it can be used without an additional rigid back protector. The system is fully electronic, requiring no physical connection to the motorcycle, and uses Dainese’s D-air algorithm to detect dangerous riding dynamics and trigger inflation in milliseconds. Dainese says the algorithm has been developed for road riding and light off-road use, which effectively rules out track use. An internal diaphragm structure is designed to distribute inflation evenly across the protected area, while the gas generator can be replaced by the user up to three times. One of the Smart GO’s more unusual features is its power supply. Rather than requiring riders to charge the airbag itself, it can draw power from a compatible USB-C smartphone that supports USB On-The-Go (OTG), or use an optional dedicated power bank. Dainese claims the latter provides up to 72 hours of riding autonomy. The system is controlled through the D-air app via Bluetooth. The Smart GO can also be paired with a dedicated 15-litre water-resistant backpack, which attaches to the vest using a magnetic fastening system. The backpack includes an organiser, a laptop compartment and an external pocket, and can be detached in seconds for use away from the bike. At £329, the Smart GO undercuts many established electronic airbag systems, although the optional accessories add to the overall cost. The dedicated power bank costs £35, a replacement gas generator is £59, and the backpack is priced at £119. Opt for the full package, and you are knocking on the door of £550 all-in. Still cheaper than most of the competition, but a slightly more expensive option than just the vest on its own. The headline price puts Dainese’s latest airbag into a more accessible bracket, while its low weight and smartphone-powered operation address two practical considerations for everyday use. How well the system works in real-world riding, particularly in terms of fit, comfort and the convenience of its power arrangements, remains to be tested and will be happening in the coming weeks – stay tuned! signals.title: Rocky Robinson set to take on Peter Hickman in land speed world record challenge
signals.summary: Peter Hickman will face stiff competition in his bid to set the outright motorcycle land speed record, with current world record holder Rocky Robinson also eyeing up a 400mph run. Rocky Robinson, the current holder of the outright motorcycle Land Speed World Record with a speed of 376.363mph, is aiming to set the first-ever 400mph run this week. Robinson will be riding the TOP 1 Ack Attack Streamliner, the same machine he set the previous record with in 2010. The TOP 1 Ack Attack Streamline will be powered by twin Suzuki Hayabusa engines, forming a combined capacity of 2,598cc. Robinson’s machine started life in a workshop in San Jose, California, back in 2003, and has since risen to land speed folklore. However, Robinson is set to face stiff competition in his bid to set a 400mph average speed by none other than 14-time Isle of Man TT winner, Peter Hickman. The road racing legend will be racing the GreyhoundLSR machine, which is also powered by Suzuki’s Hayabusa engine platform. Hickman has been heavily involved with the GreyhoundLSR team throughout the design and build of the bike, in anticipation of this week’s attempt. While Hickman has some of the most prestigious accolades in racing to his name, Robinson is a specialist when it comes to this discipline, having also broken the outright motorcycle land speed record prior to 2010; 2006 to be exact. Mike Akatiff, the designer and builder of the TOP 1 Ack Attack Streamliner, believes conditions in Bolivia are favourable for a world record attempt. “We have some real high hopes for Bolivia with that bike and with the conditions there,” Akatiff was quoted by the FIM. “Rocky wants to be the first to go over four-hundred miles an hour and we’re there to support him one-hundred per cent. “We had no fifth and sixth gear [in 2010] – it would not shift – so I don’t know how we got the record. We actually went four-hundred miles an hour right at the very end, but it’s only the timed record that counts. We have sensors on the bike that tell us the speed and we showed a little over four-hundred, but it doesn’t mean anything, it wasn’t recorded. signals.title: Kawasaki goes large with new KLE teaser
signals.summary: Kawasaki’s new teaser video seems to show a new incoming adventure bike, and all signs point to the new KLE650. Kawasaki seems to have confirmed the news that a KLE650 is on the way, after it published a new teaser video across its social media channels. As with every teaser video of this kind, not much is given away, and we do have to squint a bit and use some imagination. That said, there are some tangible things that we can see here. We’ll start with the frame. Like the KLE500 , the bike shown in the video uses a tubular trellis-style frame finished in Kawasaki’s signature metallic green colour. While it’s too early to say whether the frame is exactly the same as the one found on the existing KLE, it’s clearly still a trellis, which would tie the bike in the video to the KLE lineage. Another thing we can see, but not totally confirm, is what looks like a new engine. The right-side clutch cover is clearly very different from the existing KLE500’s. And we can also see that the clutch cover on the teaser sits much closer to the bright green frame of the bike – there is a noticeable amount of space between the clutch cover and the frame of the KLE500. What the images don’t confirm is the layout of the engine. It’s obviously going to be a single or a parallel twin, but from the teaser Kawasaki has released, we can’t accurately tell which. Another thing clearly visible is the bike’s crash bars, indicators, and auxiliary lights. The indicators are standard Kawasaki stuff and can be found on a multitude of Team Green’s bikes. The crash bars, though, tell us a bit more about the new bike. They look, from what we can see, to be identical to the ones found on the KLE500. From the gap to the indicators and the angle of the fairing behind them. Holding the two images side-by-side makes it seem like the front ends of each bike are going to be visibly very similar. The only other giveaway from the video is a quick flash of the bike’s front brake system. Unlike the KLE500, which runs a single disc, the bike in the teaser is running a twin-disc setup, with solid/fixed discs, not floating ones. The twin-disc setup is a sensible step for a bike that will likely have slightly more performance and weight than the existing KLE500. That’s about all we can glean from this one, but for more information and perhaps a more detailed look at the bike, we might not have to wait long. EICMA is just weeks away, and we’d expect to be getting a proper look at it in the flesh in Milan. signals.title: Derbyshire police officer badly injured during motorcycle theft chase
signals.summary: A police officer in Derbyshire is facing a “long road to recovery” after suffering a broken arm while stopping a motorcycle thief. An unnamed police officer has suffered a broken arm after catching a motorcycle thief who was seen stealing a Suzuki 1250 Bandit from the Royal Derby Hospital. The incident happened shortly after 8pm on Monday night, with police immediately informed of the theft, which also involved a second motorcycle. Officers making their way to the scene spotted the motorcycle in question, which had been stolen earlier that night. A pursuit then began, leading to the eventual arrest of a 19-year-old man from Derby, who was arrested on suspicion of GBH (grievous bodily harm) with intent to resist arrest and two thefts of motorcycles. However, one of the officers who captured the suspect suffered a broken arm during the ensuing struggle. The arrested man remains in custody, at the time of this writing, while the officer is currently receiving treatment. The second motorcycle in question was a bright yellow BMW R1150 GS, which was stolen from Friar Gate, near the junction with Vernon Street, at 7.10pm. Speaking about the incident, Temporary Chief Constable, Simon Blatchly, said: "I am sure the public will share my shock at the injury sustained by this officer – who was simply trying to keep our city safe and stop a criminal from escaping justice. "Each and every day officers start their shift not knowing what they will be faced with – but knowing that they may have to put their safety, and even their life, on the line. "This officer didn't think twice about running after a potentially dangerous individual, and he is now staring down the barrel of a long road to recovery. "I, along with his fellow officers and every right-minded member of our community, wish him well and hope his recovery is as quick as possible." According to the force, the BMW R1150 GS left Slack Lane, located west of the city centre, with a rider and pillion onboard. Officers are asking anyone who may have witnessed the theft, or have footage of either of the bikes being stolen, to come forward. signals.title: Suzuki’s flagship sportbike just secured its second major title
signals.summary: The Suzuki GSX-8R, first introduced in 2024, has just become a two-time championship-winning machine in the UK. After winning the 2025 British Sportbike Championship, the Suzuki GSX-8R has again proved why it’s the best middleweight bike in its segment, at least in race trim, in the UK. Powered by the company’s 776cc parallel-twin motor, the GSX-8R is closely related to the GSX-8S, which was the first model released as part of the new platform. Both bikes were later joined by the GSX-8T and GSX-8TT, a pair of modern classic twists on the well-received 8S. You might be interested in reading our Suzuki GSX-8T and GSX-8TT review . But when it comes to success for the brand’s 776cc platform, no model is enjoying more of it than the fully-faired 8R, which secured its second-straight title in the class thanks to Asher Durham and the Powerslide Suzuki team. On top of winning the 2026 title, the GSX-8R also finished third in the hands of Durham’s teammate Cameron Dawson. Suzuki GB’s marketing manager, Jak Tyrrell, said this following the company’s latest triumph: “I have to start with a big thank you to Brad [Clarke] and Dale [Coaster] at Powerslide for the effort and hard work that they have put into this season, and, of course, to Asher, who put a great championship campaign together. It’s an incredibly competitive class with fine margins, so to come away with the number of wins and podiums that he has over the course of the season speaks to his talent, too. “For us, in such a competitive class, it’s also shown just how strong the 8R package is, to win two titles in a row.” The 8R comes ready-to-ride with numerous selectable power modes, traction control, a bi-directional quickshifter, and a five-inch TFT screen as standard. Available in five different colourways, the 8R also features an OTR price of £8,999, and is currently available with a 3.9 per cent APR representative finance option. It is also included in Suzuki’s industry-leading 10-year warranty scheme. signals.title: 博世电控+KYB减震，越级配置享受高端体验｜新大洲本田NS150XC静态测评
signals.summary: 同样是150cc 踏板，为什么这台定价接近两万元的新大洲本田 NS150XC，依旧能够收获大批摩友的追捧与认可？今天，我们就从静态层面细细评鉴 NS150XC，看看它究竟值不值得入手。 NS150XC 采用硬朗的跨界 ADV 踏板造型，整体风格带有机甲越野风，前脸棱角分明，线条锋利，视觉冲击力很强；整车漆面质感细腻，外壳各部件拼接缝隙控制得比较规整，装配工艺有着不错的水准。 从侧面观察，车身运用大量几何折面切割设计，硬朗的机甲线条从前风挡一路顺延至车尾，没有繁琐多余的装饰，简约大气；前 14 寸、后 13 寸轮胎搭配长行程减震，一眼就能看出它偏向非铺装路面的跨界属性。我个人比较偏爱焕彩白配色，素车干净耐看，简约大气，后期也方便张贴各类版画或是改装，留给车主自定义的空间很充足。 接下来看灯光，前脸标志性的 X 型流水灯带是整车的点睛之笔，通电开机的动态点亮效果极具未来科技感，辨识度拉满；主光源配备两颗 LED 透镜大灯，相比普通反光碗 LED 灯，透镜结构聚光效果更好，夜间铺路能力更强，无论是夜间城市通勤，还是郊外乡村小路骑行，都可以提供不错的照明支持；日间行车灯与主灯采用分区设计，白天骑行也可以提升车辆识别度，增加骑行安全。 来到仪表方面，车辆搭载一块 5 寸 TFT 智能仪表，屏幕画面清晰，强光环境下可视效果尚可，能够展示车速、油量、水温、里程等各类日常骑行数据；不少摩友会在意仪表只显示车速、没有转速表。其实我们日常骑行，大多只需要看行驶速度，非专业测试场景下转速参考意义不大，它也不像挡车需要依据转速换挡，这项取舍可以理性看待。 此外，车机功能也十分丰富。扫描坐桶下方的二维码，即可开启投屏导航与蓝牙电话接听功能，导航信息直接投屏在仪表上，不用额外加装手机支架，破坏手把的整体感；双闪按键旁还单独设置了电话接听按键，骑行时不方便腾出手操作手机，一键接听的设计对经常通勤的摩友来说很实用。同时，前后行车记录仪在骑行中不仅可以记录沿途风景，发生事故纠纷时也能留存证据，十分方便。 关于车辆解锁的方式一共有三种：第一种是常规智能钥匙，携带钥匙靠近车辆即可感应解锁；第二种，下载官方 APP，在软件内远程解锁；第三种，手机录入对应蓝牙信息，开启蓝牙靠近车辆就能无感解锁，省去掏钥匙的麻烦，简化日常用车操作。 除了智能配置，对于踏板爱好者来说，装载储物能力也是选购踏板时的重点考量因素之一。整车没有设计前置开放式储物盒，这是因为双三星连板的设计占据了车头较大空间，但保留了双 USB 充电接口。接口布置在左手把下方，带有防尘保护盖，长途骑行时，给手机、运动相机补电会方便不少。 好在分层式坐桶有着不错的储物能力。常规状态下，前方放下一顶全盔完全没问题，后方还可以收纳雨衣、手套、充电宝这类小物件；拿掉分隔板后，也能放下羽毛球拍等偏长的物品。如果经常双人长途出行，并且两人都需要携带全盔，可以选择 NS150XC PRO 版本，原厂配备 43L 超大尾箱，箱体容积充足，单独存放一顶全盔基本没有压力，拓展载物能力更强，长途骑行也更加方便。 接下来聊聊人机三角设定。车辆座高 780mm，我身高 183 公分，体重 150 斤，坐上去视觉上会感觉车身尺寸偏小，但腿部预留空间比较宽裕，双脚平放脚踏上不会有局促感；稍微向后挪动坐姿，双脚搭在前脚踏同样舒适。这个座高适配国内多数摩友的身高：身高 175cm 左右的骑手，基本可以实现全脚掌落地；身高 165cm 的骑手，身体往前坐，前脚掌也能落地，骑行门槛相对友好。 座垫采用下沉式设计，座面填充物软硬适中，可以较好地包裹臀部。坐垫后方隆起的结构，能够在一定程度上缓解腰部疲劳，既提升骑手长时间骑行的舒适度，也可以防止后座乘员在车辆加速时向前滑动。 最后我们再来细看整车的底盘硬件配置，这也是 NS150XC 区别于同级常规踏板的核心优势，整体硬件规格十分豪华。底盘搭载 KYB 倒置 130mm 行程前减震 + KYB 双后气囊减震的旗舰级减震组合，配合专属跨界轮毂结构设计，不仅带来了充裕的离地间隙，也是 780mm 座高的重要设计前提，同时塑造出硬朗的 ADV 越野风格，和城市通勤踏板形成明显差异化。 制动层面，整车硬件同样诚意拉满。前后搭载日信高性能制动卡钳，匹配前 240mm、后 220mm 大尺寸浪花式刹车碟盘，制动基础硬件规格充足。在此之上，整车标配博世双通道 ABS + 弯道 ABS 系统，这套进阶的制动电控配置，在 150cc 小排量踏板车型中十分少见。 综合来看，近 19980 元的定价，让这台 NS150XC 拥有了同级十分出众的硬核配置。在舒适穿梭城市的同时，也具备不俗的轻度非铺装通行能力；在均衡的调校、越级硬件的加持下，既能安稳穿行城市街巷，闲暇之余也能奔赴山野，可玩性与实用性双向兼顾。如果你对踏板车的配置和品质有要求，不满足于单纯日常代步，还想体验轻度越野，这台新大洲本田 NS150XC 完全值得考虑。

signals.title: Continental introduces ContiMotion EVO, the new sport touring tyre
signals.summary: Continental introduces the ContiMotion EVO , the successor to the ContiMotion, developed for motorcyclists seeking handling, safety, and durability in everyday use. The new tyre features updated carcass materials, a silica-based hybrid compound, and EasyHandling technology, all designed to improve agility and make steering response more intuitive. The ContiMotion EVO is studied for a wide range of naked bikes, roadsters, and modern classics, including the BMW R 12 nineT, Triumph Daytona 660, Ducati Supersport 950, Honda CB650R, Suzuki GSX-8TT, and Yamaha MT-09. The new model can also be mounted in combination with the previous ContiMotion, provided compatibility specifications are met. The first sizes—17-inch front and rear tires—will be available starting in September 2026; the 190/50 ZR 17 rear tire will be available in November. signals.title: Yamaha MT-125: a new look for the 125 cc hyper naked
signals.summary: Yamaha is revamping the MT-125 for 2027, updating the design of the small hyper naked with sharper lines and a sleeker silhouette. The restyling includes a more sculpted fuel tank, a redesigned seat, and side panels with a smoked finish, accented by the MT logo. The front end also gets a makeover, featuring blade-style LED position lights, updated turn signals, and a transparent smoked fairing. The technical specifications retain the 125 cc engine with VVA technology, the Deltabox frame, and the 41 mm inverted fork. The seat height remains at 810 mm. The instrument cluster features a 5-inch TFT display, connected to a smartphone via the Yamaha MyRide app and equipped with integrated navigation featuring turn-by-turn directions, as well as call, music, and message management. The color lineup includes Ice Storm, Icon Blue, Tech Black, and the new Redline White, featuring high-contrast graphics and a two-tone seat. The 2027 Yamaha MT-125 will arrive at dealerships in the first quarter of 2027. signals.title: Bagster at EICMA 2026: bags, seats, and new mounting solutions
signals.summary: Bagster will be at EICMA 2026 showcasing new products dedicated to transport, comfort, and protection for motorcycles and scooters. The star of the show will be Fastlane , a new collection of bags featuring a sporty and modular design, designed for roadsters, hypernaked bikes, and sport-touring models. The range includes backpacks, tank bags, rear bags, and side bags, along with dedicated accessories. Also on display will be AIM’ON , a magneto-mechanical mounting system designed to simplify the installation and removal of compatible tank bags, and the Sit’n Go complete seats, handcrafted in Normandy to enhance comfort for both rider and passenger. For tank protection, there’s Triple Black, a new design that combines materials, textures, and shades of black. There’s also gear for the cold season, including the Winzip and Boomerang leg covers for scooters, the Towear wearable model, and the Exxel Pro and Boxfirst hand warmers. signals.title: Kabuto, engineering tomorrow's helmets with Japanese craftsmanship
signals.summary: At Hall 7, Stand C24 , the Japanese helmet brand will welcome motorcycle enthusiasts, industry professionals and trade visitors with an exhibition bringing together its latest innovations, racing heritage and a design philosophy rooted in Japanese craftsmanship. One of the main highlights of Kabuto’s presence at EICMA 2026 will be the debut of the all-new KF-2F , the brand’s next- generation racing-derived full-face helmet featuring FIM FRHPhe-02 homologation, Mips and Quin technology. Kabuto will also present its premium Carbon Series , showcasing the brand’s approach to combining advanced materials, lightweight construction and distinctive aesthetics. On this regards, the exhibition will feature two models: F-17R, a carbon-fiber interpretation of Kabuto’s F-17 racing full-face helmet and Geosys-R, bringing carbon-fiber construction to the brand's adventure-touring helmet platform. Urban mobility and touring will also be represented by the Exceed , a compact open-face helmet featuring an integrated sunshade, presented at EICMA with a new concept colour scheme. The Ryuki modular helmet combines the convenience of a flip-up design with aerodynamic styling, an integrated sunshade and practical features developed for everyday riding and touring. signals.title: Desner T30, the new microcar with premium features
signals.summary: Desner , the electric microcar brand by ITB Auto S.r.l., is officially rolling out the T30, the very first premium L6e model in their lineup. Demo cars will be hitting dealership floors over the next few weeks, with the first official registrations set for December. The brand's growing dealer network already spans over 35 locations, with ambitious plans to cross the 60-dealership mark by 2027. The T30 is an agile, all-electric light quadricycle that lets drivers get behind the wheel starting at just 14 years old with an AM license , capping its top speed at 45 kilometers per hour. Compact yet surprisingly spacious, this two-seater with three doors measures 2.92 meters long, 1.50 meters wide, and weighs in at a lightweight 417 kilograms empty. Powered by rear-wheel drive, its permanent magnet synchronous motor delivers a nominal 5 kilowatts—surging up to a 14-kilowatt peak—alongside 75 Newton-meters of torque. Its 8-kilowatt-hour battery offers an impressive declared range of up to 150 kilometers on the NEDC cycle, taking roughly 8 hours for a full charge using a standard household socket or a public charging station via an adapter. When it comes to comfort and safety, the T30 doesn't hold back. It comes packed with standard features including airbags, air conditioning, a 7-inch LCD display, a rearview camera, power windows, and remote central locking, all wrapped in a sleek palette of black, white, and grey. Desner is also making waves at EICMA, showcasing the Y300 MY2027 , an L7e heavy quadricycle designed for drivers 16 and older with a B1 license. signals.title: The irresistible charm of the Honda CBR500R Four
signals.summary: Honda is expanding its super sport family with the brand-new CBR500R Four, a motorcycle engineered around an inline-four engine designed to bridge traditional Japanese supersport character with cutting-edge technology, making spirited riding accessible to younger riders. At its heart lies a 500 cc DOHC 16-valve engine —an evolution of the 400 cc unit found in the Asian-market CB400 Super Four—pushing out 72 horsepower at 11,000 rpm and a peak torque of 47.4 Nm at 9,750 rpm, with the redline set at 12,500 rpm. This configuration promises a lively power delivery and the signature high-revving rush typical of four-cylinder powerplants. Advanced technical highlights include Nickel-Silicon Carbide (Ni-SiC) cylinder bore plating, Diamond-Like Carbon (DLC) coated valve tappets, dual ram-air intakes, and a high-efficiency downdraft intake system. A 35 kW variant compliant with the A2 license will also be available. The engine is paired with a six-speed transmission via Honda’s electronic E-Clutch system. Throttle By Wire electronic throttle control offers three preset riding modes and two customizable ones. The steel diamond-frame chassis uses the engine as a stressed member, complemented by a 41 mm inverted KYB fork up front, while an aluminum swingarm at the rear works with a Pro-Link progressive linkage monoshock, adjustable for spring preload across five positions. The braking system features a dual-channel ABS, front radial Nissin two-piston calipers, and dual 296 mm discs. Rounding out the equipment are a 5-inch full-color TFT display, Honda RoadSync connectivity, and a USB-C port. Two striking color schemes are offered: Ignition Red , featuring the iconic HRC Tricolour livery with bold Honda graphics, and Mat Ballistic Black Metallic for a stealthy, total-black aesthetic. signals.summary: Jadwal MotoGP Australia 2026, Rangkaian Balapan Dimulai Hari Ini JAKARTA, KOMPAS.com MotoGP Australia 2026 mulai bergulir di Sirkuit Phillip Island, Jumat (23/10/2026). Seri ini menjadi kesempatan bagi para pebalap untuk mengumpulkan poin sekaligus memperbaiki posisi di klasemen sementara kejuaraan dunia. Sorotan tertuju pada Jorge Martin dan Marc Marquez yang tengah bersaing ketat di papan atas. Martin masih memimpin klasemen dengan 355 poin, hanya terpaut dua poin dari Marquez yang mengoleksi 353 poin. Keduanya datang ke Australia setelah mendapatkan hasil berbeda pada MotoGP Indonesia di Sirkuit Mandalika. Martin finis di posisi ketiga, sedangkan Marquez menuntaskan balapan di urutan keenam. Baca juga: Cegah Kebakaran, Modifikasi Lampu Mobil Wajib Kabel Anti-Bakar Hasil tersebut membuat persaingan perebutan gelar juara dunia masih terbuka. Terlebih, Marco Bezzecchi yang menempati peringkat ketiga dengan 309 poin juga menunjukkan performa kompetitif setelah memenangi balapan di Mandalika. Pada seri Australia, para pebalap akan menjalani sesi latihan bebas dan kualifikasi sebelum mengikuti Sprint Race pada Sabtu (24/10/2026). Balapan utama dijadwalkan berlangsung pada Minggu (25/10/2026). Twitter/MotoGP Pembalap Trackhouse Racing, Raul Fernandez, mencetak kemenangan perdana di kelas utama MotoGP setelah tampil konsisten di Sirkuit Phillip Island, Australia, Minggu (19/10/2025). Sirkuit Phillip Island juga menyimpan catatan positif bagi Raul Fernandez. Pebalap Trackhouse MotoGP tersebut berhasil memenangi MotoGP Australia 2025, sekaligus mencatatkan kemenangan pertamanya di kelas utama. Kemenangan itu juga menjadi yang pertama bagi tim Trackhouse di MotoGP. Fernandez finis di depan Fabio Di Giannantonio yang menempati posisi kedua. signals.title: Indonesia Ikut Proyek Personalisasi Omoda X Global
signals.summary: Indonesia Ikut Proyek Personalisasi Omoda X Global WUHU, KOMPAS.com Pengguna Omoda dari Indonesia ikut berpartisipasi dalam Omoda X Co-Creation Project, program yang memberikan ruang bagi konsumen untuk mengekspresikan karakter personal melalui modifikasi dan personalisasi kendaraan. Program tersebut diperkenalkan dalam acara Omoda X Night yang menjadi bagian dari Omoda & Jaecoo International User Summit di Wuhu, China. Selain Indonesia, pengguna dari Brasil, Afrika Selatan, dan Polandia turut menampilkan interpretasi Omoda X berdasarkan latar budaya, minat, serta kreativitas masing-masing. Melalui proyek ini, Omoda ingin menunjukkan bagaimana kendaraan dapat menjadi sarana ekspresi penggunanya. Keterlibatan konsumen dari berbagai negara juga membawa perspektif lokal dalam pengembangan personalisasi kendaraan. Baca juga: Cegah Kebakaran, Modifikasi Lampu Mobil Wajib Kabel Anti-Bakar Dalam kesempatan yang sama, Omoda & Jaecoo turut memaparkan rencana pengembangan teknologi untuk sejumlah model globalnya. Salah satunya adalah teknologi hybrid electric vehicle (HEV) dengan baterai berkapasitas 5 kWh yang akan pertama kali diterapkan pada Omoda O7. Selain itu, perusahaan menyiapkan pelapis insulasi panas untuk Omoda O4. Teknologi tersebut ditujukan untuk membantu menjaga kenyamanan suhu di dalam kabin. Sementara itu, Jaecoo J5 dan Jaecoo J7 akan mendapatkan teknologi SIVP (Super Intelligent Valet Parking). Fitur ini dikembangkan untuk mempermudah proses parkir kendaraan. signals.title: Motor Biasa Pakai Pertamax Lalu Beralih ke Pertalite, Apa Risikonya?
signals.summary: Motor Biasa Pakai Pertamax Lalu Beralih ke Pertalite, Apa Risikonya? JAKARTA, KOMPAS.com - Penggunaan bahan bakar minyak (BBM) yang lebih murah sering menjadi pilihan pengendara sepeda motor untuk menekan pengeluaran harian. Salah satu cara yang kerap dilakukan adalah beralih dari Pertamax ke Pertalite , yang memiliki harga lebih terjangkau. Namun, apakah pergantian bahan bakar tersebut berdampak pada performa dan kondisi mesin? 2W Service Head PT Suzuki Indomobil Sales (SIS) Victor Assani mengatakan, penggunaan BBM dengan RON lebih rendah dapat langsung memengaruhi kinerja kendaraan dalam jangka pendek. Baca juga: Cegah Kebakaran, Modifikasi Lampu Mobil Wajib Kabel Anti-Bakar KOMPAS.com/FINDI RAKMENI Ilustrasi motor mengisi BBM. "Penggunaan BBM dengan RON yang lebih rendah dalam jangka pendek dapat kita rasakan langsung pada kinerjanya. Tenaga pada kendaraan akan terasa tidak pada performa terbaiknya seperti pada akselerasi dan power, atau kadang kita merasakan getaran yang tidak sewajarnya pada kemudi," kata Victor saat dihubungi Kompas.com, baru-baru ini. Menurut Victor, kendaraan modern memiliki sistem yang dapat menyesuaikan waktu pengapian agar mesin tetap bekerja dengan aman ketika menggunakan BBM yang nilai oktannya tidak sesuai dengan rekomendasi. Namun, penyesuaian tersebut bisa membuat performa mesin menurun, misalnya akselerasi terasa kurang responsif. Baca juga: Efek Mobil Listrik, Tren Modifikasi Lampu Mobil Kini Berubah Selain itu, konsumsi BBM juga berpotensi meningkat sehingga penghematan dari penggunaan bahan bakar yang lebih murah belum tentu sebesar yang diharapkan. Ini yang mengakibatkan kondisi yang tadi disebutkan di atas muncul, termasuk merembet ke konsumsi bahan bakar yang lebih tinggi, ucapnya. KOMPAS.Com/Erik Alfian Warga Balikpapan melakukan pengisian Pertalite di SPBU Gunung Guntur Balikpapan Tengah. Kota Balikpapan resmi mendapat tambaha kuota Pertalite sebesar 1.250 KL dari BPH Migas. Selain penurunan performa, penggunaan BBM dengan RON yang tidak sesuai kebutuhan mesin juga dapat meningkatkan risiko terjadinya knocking atau suara mengelitik. Victor menjelaskan, knocking yang terjadi secara berulang bisa menimbulkan benturan dan tekanan yang tidak semestinya pada komponen mesin. "Efek dari ini semua adalah terjadinya gesekan atau benturan antara piston dengan dinding silinder secara kasar. Muara dari ini adalah timbulnya suara mengelitik pada mesin atau dalam bahasa kerennya adalah knocking," ucap Victor. Jika berlangsung terus-menerus, kondisi tersebut berpotensi meningkatkan risiko kerusakan komponen, seperti dinding silinder, piston, ring piston, katup, hingga kepala silinder. "Ujungnya, kita akan menanggung beban kerusakan termasuk risiko pergantian komponen yang bisa dikatakan cukup banyak dan akumulasinya mahal," katanya. Karena itu, Victor menyarankan pengendara untuk memilih BBM sesuai dengan rekomendasi pabrikan yang tercantum dalam buku manual kendaraan. Kebutuhan RON setiap motor dapat berbeda, bergantung pada spesifikasi dan rancangan mesinnya. Jika ingin menekan biaya operasional, pengendara dapat menerapkan gaya berkendara yang efisien, memilih rute perjalanan yang lebih efektif, serta mengurangi perjalanan yang tidak mendesak.
